intro: Engineering Competencies (ECs) are expected to be demonstrated by graduates during their practical experiences, which have been mapped with PLOs to reflect integration in the designed curriculum.

items.label: EC1 Comprehend and Apply Universal Knowledge:
items.text: Comprehend and apply advanced Engineering knowledge of the widely-applied principles underpinning good practices.

items.label: EC2 Comprehend and Apply Local Knowledge:
items.text: Comprehend and apply advanced Engineering knowledge of the widely-applied principles underpinning good practice specific to the jurisdiction of practices.

items.label: EC3 Problem Analysis:
items.text: Define, investigate and analyze complex Engineering problems using data and information technologies where applicable.

items.label: EC4 Design and Development of Solutions:
items.text: Design or develop solutions to complex Engineering problems, considering a variety of perspectives and taking account of stakeholder views.

items.label: EC5 Evaluation:
items.text: Evaluate the outcomes and impacts of complex Engineering activities.

items.label: EC6 Protection of Society:
items.text: Recognize the foreseeable economic, social, and environmental effects of complex Engineering activities and seek to achieve sustainable outcomes.

items.label: EC7 Legal, Regulatory, and Cultural:
items.text: Meet all legal, regulatory, and cultural requirements and protect public health and safety in the course of all Engineering activities.

items.label: EC9 Manage Engineering Activities:
items.text: Manage part or all of one or more complex Engineering activities.

items.label: EC10 Communication and Collaboration:
items.text: Communicate and collaborate using multiple media clearly and inclusively with a broad range of stakeholders in the course of all Engineering activities.

items.label: EC11 Continuing Professional Development (CPD) and Lifelong Learning:
items.text: Undertake CPD activities to maintain and extend competences and enhance the ability to adapt to emerging technologies and the ever-changing nature of work.

items.label: EC12 Judgment:
items.text: Recognize complexity and assess alternatives in light of competing requirements and incomplete knowledge. Exercise sound judgement in the course of all complex Engineering activities.

items.label: EC13 Responsibility for Decisions:
items.text: Be responsible for making decisions on part or all of complex Engineering activities.
